title: No advantage from classical assistance for energy-constrained bosonic dephasing channels
abstract: We prove that four capacities of single-mode bosonic dephasing channels coincide under an average photon-number constraint: the unassisted quantum capacity, the unassisted private capacity, the two-way classically assisted quantum capacity, and the two-way public-classically assisted private capacity. The assistance may be interactive: the parties can exchange classical messages between channel uses and choose subsequent inputs based on earlier outcomes. For every finite value of the constraint, their common value is the coherent information optimized over Fock-diagonal input states satisfying the constraint. The proof uses a relative entropy comparison with the completely dephasing channel to derive chain rules for the Rains relative entropy and the relative entropy of entanglement. These chain rules give an upper bound on the rates achievable by adaptive protocols whose mean input photon number is constrained on average over all channel uses. We also show that both chain rules are attained by canonical purifications of finite-energy Fock-diagonal states.
summary: This theoretical work proves that for bosonic dephasing channels, the quantum and private communication capacities are robust against classical assistance when an average photon-number constraint is active. The key finding is that these capacities are determined by optimizing the coherent information over constrained Fock-diagonal input states. This establishes a fundamental limit on information transfer in noisy bosonic quantum channels.
main_problem: The paper proves the coincidence of four different communication capacities (quantum, private, and their classically assisted variants) for single-mode bosonic dephasing channels when an average photon-number constraint is imposed.
main_result: Under the average photon-number constraint, all four capacities are equal to the coherent information optimized over Fock-diagonal input states satisfying that constraint.
method: The proof utilizes relative entropy comparisons with the completely dephasing channel to derive chain rules for Rains relative entropy and the relative entropy of entanglement, bounding achievable rates for adaptive protocols.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is a single-mode bosonic dephasing channel acting on bosonic input states, constrained by a finite average photon number E.
key_observables: Quantum capacity (Q), private capacity (P), coherent information ($I_c$), Rains relative entropy, and relative entropy of entanglement.
important_parameters: The average photon-number constraint E, which must be finite.
main_assumptions: The result holds for any finite constraint E, and the analysis extends to countably supported photon-number distributions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the capacity equality by first deriving relative entropy bounds using comparisons with the completely dephasing channel, then applying these bounds to prove the capacity theorems for both quantum and private communication.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on information transmission rates through realistic noisy bosonic channels, directly impacting the design of quantum communication protocols.
